outcome: neonatal morbidity (composite of oxygen therapy/ventilation need, respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of the newborn, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, intraventricular hemorrhage grade III/IV, neonatal mortality)
cohort: The study included growth-restricted fetuses delivered at 34+0 to 36+6 weeks gestational age at a tertiary university-affiliated hospital between March 2016 and March 2022.
finding: Antenatal corticosteroids did not significantly lower the rate of the primary composite neonatal morbidity outcome in late preterm pregnancies with small-for-gestational-age fetuses, although hypoglycemia was more common among ACS-exposed neonates.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite neonatal morbidity outcome.
